query: Reported superconducting high-entropy alloys are dominated by Nb-Ta matrices, while other studies concern titanium-rich systems based on heavy transition metals and partly ordered systems. Consequently, these precedents do not establish what controls superconductivity in high-entropy alloys outside the best-studied material classes. Within the defining constraint of a solid solution containing at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent each, what governs superconducting behavior in such an uncharacterized high-entropy alloy, and why? State one testable mechanistic hypothesis, a controlled comparison against the starting material, predicted observations relative to the baseline, applicable boundary conditions, the earlier evidence supporting the hypothesis, and an outcome that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: In high-entropy alloys (HEAs) outside the well‐studied Nb–Ta and titanium‐rich systems, superconductivity is primarily governed by the degree of local lattice distortion induced by chemical disorder. These distortions modify the phonon spectrum and thereby modulate the electron–phonon coupling strength, which in turn sets the superconducting transition temperature (Tc).
generation.material_initial_state: A uniformly mixed solid solution HEA containing at least five elements (each at ≥5 atomic percent) in a single-phase structure with minimal secondary phase formation.
generation.intervention: Systematically vary the alloy composition to increase or decrease the average difference in atomic radii among the constituent elements while keeping the overall elemental percentages within the specified limit. Process all samples under identical annealing conditions to ensure equilibrium.
generation.conditions: Samples are annealed in an inert atmosphere (e.g., argon) at a moderate temperature (e.g., 800–1000°C) for a fixed time to achieve homogeneity, then measured at cryogenic temperatures around the expected Tc.
generation.structural_mediator: Local lattice distortions (strain and deviations from perfect crystallinity) induced by differences in atomic sizes among the multiple elements.
generation.mechanism: Atomic size differences in the HEA lead to local lattice distortions that alter the phonon dispersion (phonon softening). Enhanced electron–phonon coupling in regions with higher distortion increases the pairing strength, thus raising the superconducting transition temperature.
generation.predicted_outcome: HEA samples with an increased average variance in atomic radii (and hence larger local lattice distortions) will show a measurable enhancement in Tc compared to a baseline HEA with minimal size dispersion. The effect is expected to be evident up to an optimal distortion level beyond which detrimental scattering might counteract the benefit.
generation.baseline: A reference HEA synthesized to have the least atomic size disparity possible (for example, an alloy designed to mimic the low distortion seen in Nb–Ta systems) under the same processing conditions.
generation.boundary: This mechanism is expected to hold in single-phase, fully miscible solid solution HEAs. It may not apply if phase segregation, ordering, or formation of secondary phases occurs, or if the compositional constraints (at least five elements at no less than 5 atomic percent) are not maintained.
generation.uncertainty: The quantitative relationship between the magnitude of local lattice distortions, the degree of phonon softening, and the consequent change in Tc is not precisely known. Additionally, possible counteracting effects of disorder-induced electron scattering on superconductivity remain uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare a series of HEA samples while systematically varying the constituent elements to control the average atomic size variance. Process all samples under identical annealing and cooling conditions. Measure Tc using four-probe resistance measurements and use techniques such as high-resolution X-ray diffraction (XRD) and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) to assess local lattice distortions.
measurements: Superconducting transition temperature (Tc) from resistance vs. temperature curves
Quantitative metrics for lattice distortions (e.g., peak broadening in XRD, local strain measurements via TEM)
Electron–phonon coupling estimates (if available via spectroscopic methods)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the degree of local lattice distortion does not correlate with changes in Tc—specifically, if samples with increased atomic size variance (and measured lattice distortion) do not show an enhanced Tc relative to the baseline HEA—the hypothesis would be falsified.
